source_text: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν, ὁ γνωστικός, ὁ μιμούμενος τὸν θεὸν καθ’ ὅσον οἷόν τε, μηδὲν παραλιπὼν τῶν εἰς τὴν ἐνδεχομένην ὁμοίωσιν, ἐγκρατευόμενος, ὑπομένων, δικαίως βιούς. βασιλεύων τῶν παθῶν, μεταδιδοὺς ὧν ἔχει, ὡς οἷός τέ ἐστιν, εὐεργετῶν καὶ λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ. οὗτος μέγιστος, φησίν, ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ ὃς ἂν ποιῇ καὶ διδάσκῃ μιμούμενος τὸν θεὸν τῷ παραπλήσια χαρίζεσθαι· κοινωφελεῖς γὰρ αἱ τοῦ θεοῦ δωρεαί.
pass_a_gloss: This is the one according to image and likeness, the one knowing, the one imitating God insofar as it is possible, leaving out nothing of the things into the possible likeness, being self-controlled, enduring, living righteously, reigning over the passions, sharing what he has, as much as he is able, doing good by word and deed. This one is greatest, he says, in the kingdom, whoever does and teaches, imitating God, giving graciously in a similar manner; for the gifts of God are for the common benefit.
pass_b_english: This is the one who bears the image and likeness of God, the one who truly knows, the one who imitates God as far as it is possible, omitting nothing that belongs to that attainable likeness: he is self-controlled, he endures, he lives righteously. He reigns over his passions; he shares what he has, to the extent he is able, doing good both in word and in deed. He, the text declares, is greatest in the kingdom: whoever acts and teaches in this way, imitating God by giving graciously in like manner, for the gifts of God are given for the common benefit.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both accurately capture the Greek text. Pass B's addition of 'of God' to 'image and likeness' and 'the text declares' for 'φησίν' are acceptable stylistic expansions that do not alter the meaning or add new doctrine. The translation of 'κοινωφελεῖς αἱ τοῦ θεοῦ δωρεαί' as 'the gifts of God are for the common benefit' (A) and 'the gifts of God are given for the common benefit' (B) is faithful to the sense.
